title: 14.3 A 28nm 17.83-to-62.84TFLOPS/W Broadcast-Alignment Floating-Point CIM Macro with Non-Two's-Complement MAC for CNNs and Transformers
problem: Floating-point neural network inference requires high precision but incurs significant energy/area overhead vs. integer quantization; floating-point CIM (compute-in-memory) faces challenges: (1) alignment operations conflict with CIM's parallel structure, (2) peripheral alignment circuits add area/power, (3) 2's-complement MAC wastes cycles on negative-weight sparsity and sign-bit overhead.
motivation: FP precision needed for transformer models and edge AI inference; standard digital FP-MAC is inefficient; CIM offers better P/W but prior FP-CIM designs sacrifice accuracy (BF16 quantization loss) or add complexity. Non-2's-complement approach could exploit high negative-weight sparsity in neural networks.
method: Broadcast-Alignment (B-A) floating-point CIM macro with embedded lightweight convertor for BF16/INT8 MAC operations. Broadcast input + embedded adaptive-alignment scheme with dual-bit serial MAC. Non-2's-complement (N2CMAC) MAC format reduces dynamic circuit activity and sign-bit overhead. Format-mixed approach supports BF16 and INT8 in same macro.
key_novelty: Broadcast input architecture with embedded lightweight convertor enabling high input reusability in FP-CIM; Non-2's-complement MAC exploiting negative-weight sparsity.
contributions: Broadcast-alignment FP-CIM macro with improved input reusability for BF16/INT8
Embedded lightweight convertor (area-efficient vs. parallel peripheral schemes)
Dual-bit serial MAC for area efficiency
Format-mixed N2CMAC reducing dynamic energy and sign-bit overhead
Measured: 62.84 TFLOPS/W for BF16, 90.15 TOPS/W for INT8
baselines: Prior FP-CIM designs with peripheral alignment (higher area/power)
Digital FP32 MAC (much lower energy efficiency)
Integer-only CIM (lower accuracy for FP-critical models)
limitations: Abstract does not provide area comparison, latency per inference, or accuracy comparison (FP32 baseline). Real CNN/transformer benchmark results not shown.
primary_theme: Efficient floating-point CIM with broadcast alignment and non-2's-complement MAC
